entries.title: I Samuel 17:1
segments: Shochoh; a place in Judah between fifteen and eighteen miles south-west from Jerusalem, having a valley north of it, which is believed to be the ancient valley of Elah.  Azekah and Ephes-dammim were near to Shochoh.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:2
segments: By the valley of Elah; on the north side of it.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:4
segments: Whose height was six cubits and a span; a cubit was about eighteen inches, and a span about nine inches.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:5
segments:
Coat of mail; in the original, a coat of mail of scales; that is, made of thin plates of metal overlapping each other like the scales of a fish. 
 
  Five thousand shekels; nearly two hundred pounds.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:6
segments: Target; a smaller shield suspended between his shoulders, to be used when occasion might require.  The larger shield was carried before him by his armor-bearer.  Some, however, prefer to understand a javelin hung by a strap behind his back.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:7
segments: Six hundred shekels; about twenty-five pounds.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:10
segments: When distinguished strength and courage make men proud, adn lead them to trust in themselves and despise others, they often become the occasion of their ruin.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:12
segments: That Ephrathite of Beth-lehem-judah; so called from Ephratah, one of the names of Bethlehem.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:17
segments: Men in executing their projects often have no idea of the ends which God by them will accomplish.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:22
segments: Carriage; the articles which he had brought with him.  Carriage, in the old English use of the word, signifies baggage, vessels, etc., that one carries with him in journeying.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:25
segments:
Free; free from taxes and public burdens. 
 
Men are induced to perform much labor, and make many sacrifices, by the hope of reward; and God graciously points us to the joy set before us, as a motive to deny ourselves, take up the cross, and follow Christ.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:28
segments: Men naturally envy those who do better and are more honored than themselves, and no ties of relationship are any certain security against the effects of this evil and malignant passion.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:32
segments: Confidence in God is a source of the highest and noblest courage, the most self-sacrificing devotion to duty, and the most exalted virtue.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:34
segments: Past experience of the readiness and power of God to help, encourages men to trust in him, and to expect from him in future all which they need.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:38
segments: The devices and efforts of men to aid us often prove a hinderance instead of a help, and we must renounce dependence on them and depend on God in our efforts, in order to meet with success.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:39
segments:
Assayed; attempted. 
 
  Not proved them; not been accustomed to them, and could not readily use them.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:40
segments: True dependence on God leads men not to neglect appropriate means, but in the right way to use them.  Thus, while they work, God works by them in securing the result, and preparing them to give him the glory.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:43
segments: Pride goeth before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:45
segments: In the name of the Lord; by his direction, with confidence in him, and for the purpose of promoting his cause.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:46
segments: One great design of Jehovah in all his dealings, is to make known his character, and show to the universe that there is no one but himself who governs and controls in the kingdoms of nature, providence, and grace.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:51
segments: The strongest as well as the weakest are dependent upon God, and that expectation which rests on creatures is liable at any time to be disappointed.

entries.title: I Samuel 17:55
segments: Services performed for men may by them be forgotten, and those who render them pass out of mind; but services done for God he always remembers, and will graciously reward.
